MC	<p>9933_b8b2</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Two Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the between a single pair of genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among two genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #036a73;">Gene A</span></strong> is related to the '<span style="color: #036a73;"><i>amber</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #036a73;">Gene A</span> cells develop a rich yellow-orange pigmentation, giving the colony a warm, amber hue.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #7f38a2;">Gene P</span></strong> is connected with the '<span style="color: #7f38a2;"><i>pebble</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #7f38a2;">Gene P</span> produces colonies with a rough, uneven surface that resembles a collection of tiny pebbles.</li> </ul><table style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><tr><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 2px;"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="156" height="120" viewBox="0 0 122 94" role="img" aria-label="Unordered ascus: ++, ap, ++, ap"><desc>Each recessive allele contributes its own color; plus alleles remain neutral. MC	<p>7776_2091</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Two Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the between a single pair of genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among two genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #006d61;">Gene M</span></strong> is analogous to the '<span style="color: #006d61;"><i>militant</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #006d61;">Gene M</span> colonies are small, dense, and secrete compounds that inhibit the growth of nearby colonies.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #6141c2;">Gene W</span></strong> is correlated with the '<span style="color: #6141c2;"><i>webbed</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #6141c2;">Gene W</span> colonies produce delicate, web-like strands that connect neighboring colonies in a cobweb pattern.</li> </ul><table style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><tr><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 2px;"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="156" height="120" viewBox="0 0 122 94" role="img" aria-label="Unordered ascus: ++, mw, ++, mw"><desc>Each recessive allele contributes its own color; plus alleles remain neutral. MC	<p>1ae2_354b</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Two Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the between a single pair of genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among two genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #904610;">Gene A</span></strong> is related to the '<span style="color: #904610;"><i>amber</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #904610;">Gene A</span> cells develop a rich yellow-orange pigmentation, giving the colony a warm, amber hue.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #006d61;">Gene B</span></strong> is linked with the '<span style="color: #006d61;"><i>bubbly</i></span>' phenotype. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among two genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #006886;">Gene F</span></strong> is linked with the '<span style="color: #006886;"><i>fuzzy</i></span>' phenotype. MC	<p>bd63_b130</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Two Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the between a single pair of genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among two genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #7f5411;">Gene H</span></strong> is correlated with the '<span style="color: #7f5411;"><i>hairy</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #7f5411;">Gene H</span> cells develop long, thread-like filaments that extend outward, creating a hairy, shaggy texture on the colony.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #0062a0;">Gene N</span></strong> is analogous to the '<span style="color: #0062a0;"><i>nude</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #0062a0;">Gene N</span> cells have an unusually smooth surface with no visible external features or textures.</li> </ul><table style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><tr><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 2px;"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="156" height="120" viewBox="0 0 122 94" role="img" aria-label="Unordered ascus: ++, hn, ++, hn"><desc>Each recessive allele contributes its own color; plus alleles remain neutral. MC	<p>600f_4ab8</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Two Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the between a single pair of genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among two genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #715c00;">Gene K</span></strong> is associated with the '<span style="color: #715c00;"><i>knotted</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #715c00;">Gene K</span> cells grow in twisted, coiled shapes, resulting in a knotted or gnarled appearance.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #6141c2;">Gene N</span></strong> is affiliated with the '<span style="color: #6141c2;"><i>nude</i></span>' phenotype. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among two genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #715c00;">Gene B</span></strong> is linked with the '<span style="color: #715c00;"><i>bubbly</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #715c00;">Gene B</span> produces excessive gas bubbles during growth, causing foamy appearance of the media.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #8f377b;">Gene H</span></strong> is analogous to the '<span style="color: #8f377b;"><i>hairy</i></span>' phenotype. MC	<p>d22a_ede2</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Two Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the between a single pair of genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among two genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #904610;">Gene C</span></strong> is affiliated with the '<span style="color: #904610;"><i>clumpy</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #904610;">Gene C</span> grows in dense, irregular clusters, with cells clumping together rather than spreading smoothly.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #6141c2;">Gene Y</span></strong> is correlated with the '<span style="color: #6141c2;"><i>yolk</i></span>' phenotype. MC	<p>21e0_0381</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Two Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the between a single pair of genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among two genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #006886;">Gene J</span></strong> is correlated with the '<span style="color: #006886;"><i>jeweled</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #006886;">Gene J</span> colonies appear dotted with tiny, iridescent spots that sparkle under light.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #8f377b;">Gene Y</span></strong> is associated with the '<span style="color: #8f377b;"><i>yolk</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #8f377b;">Gene Y</span> cells develop a dense, yellowish core that resembles an egg yolk when viewed under a microscope.</li> </ul><table style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><tr><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 2px;"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="156" height="120" viewBox="0 0 122 94" role="img" aria-label="Unordered ascus: ++, jy, ++, jy"><desc>Each recessive allele contributes its own color; plus alleles remain neutral. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among two genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #3c6c29;">Gene P</span></strong> is analogous to the '<span style="color: #3c6c29;"><i>pebble</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #3c6c29;">Gene P</span> produces colonies with a rough, uneven surface that resembles a collection of tiny pebbles.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #6141c2;">Gene T</span></strong> is connected with the '<span style="color: #6141c2;"><i>toxic</i></span>' phenotype. MC	<p>161f_207e</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Two Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the between a single pair of genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among two genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #7f5411;">Gene E</span></strong> is associated with the '<span style="color: #7f5411;"><i>elephant</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #7f5411;">Gene E</span> cells absorb excessive amounts of liquid, resulting in giant, swollen cells.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #6141c2;">Gene T</span></strong> is related to the '<span style="color: #6141c2;"><i>toxic</i></span>' phenotype. MC	<p>bd3e_3467</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Two Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the between a single pair of genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among two genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #7f5411;">Gene N</span></strong> is related to the '<span style="color: #7f5411;"><i>nude</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #7f5411;">Gene N</span> cells have an unusually smooth surface with no visible external features or textures.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #006d61;">Gene W</span></strong> is linked with the '<span style="color: #006d61;"><i>webbed</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #006d61;">Gene W</span> colonies produce delicate, web-like strands that connect neighboring colonies in a cobweb pattern.</li> </ul><table style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><tr><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 2px;"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="156" height="120" viewBox="0 0 122 94" role="img" aria-label="Unordered ascus: ++, nw, ++, nw"><desc>Each recessive allele contributes its own color; plus alleles remain neutral. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among two genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #715c00;">Gene D</span></strong> is connected with the '<span style="color: #715c00;"><i>doubled</i></span>' phenotype. MC	<p>163e_c62c</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Two Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the between a single pair of genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among two genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #9c392d;">Gene C</span></strong> is linked with the '<span style="color: #9c392d;"><i>clumpy</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #9c392d;">Gene C</span> grows in dense, irregular clusters, with cells clumping together rather than spreading smoothly.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #006886;">Gene K</span></strong> is correlated with the '<span style="color: #006886;"><i>knotted</i></span>' phenotype. MC	<p>0a7b_a444</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Two Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the between a single pair of genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among two genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #166e49;">Gene A</span></strong> is correlated with the '<span style="color: #166e49;"><i>amber</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #166e49;">Gene A</span> cells develop a rich yellow-orange pigmentation, giving the colony a warm, amber hue.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #3456b9;">Gene X</span></strong> is connected with the '<span style="color: #3456b9;"><i>xenon</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #3456b9;">Gene X</span> cells emit a faint glow under UV light, as if they were fluorescent.</li> </ul><table style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><tr><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 2px;"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="156" height="120" viewBox="0 0 122 94" role="img" aria-label="Unordered ascus: ++, ax, ++, ax"><desc>Each recessive allele contributes its own color; plus alleles remain neutral. style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 5px 8px;">6,400</td></tr></table><h6>Step-by-Step Instructions</h6><ul> <li>Step 1: Find the row for the Parental Type for all three genes.</li> <li>Step 2: Looking at only your two genes, assign PD, NPD, TT.</li> <li>Step 3: Determine if the two genes are linked.</li> <ul><li>PD &gt;&gt; NPD &rarr; linked; PD &approx; NPD &rarr; unlinked</li></ul> <li>Step 4: Determine the map distance between the two genes.</li> <ul><li>D = &half; (TT + 6 NPD) / total = (3 NPD + &half; TT) / total</li></ul></ul><h5>Determine the distance between the two genes MC	<p>6496_056a</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Two Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the between a single pair of genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among two genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #7f5411;">Gene B</span></strong> is linked with the '<span style="color: #7f5411;"><i>bubbly</i></span>' phenotype. MC	<p>49e6_2d5d</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Two Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the between a single pair of genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among two genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #3c6c29;">Gene C</span></strong> is correlated with the '<span style="color: #3c6c29;"><i>clumpy</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #3c6c29;">Gene C</span> grows in dense, irregular clusters, with cells clumping together rather than spreading smoothly.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #3456b9;">Gene W</span></strong> is correlated with the '<span style="color: #3456b9;"><i>webbed</i></span>' phenotype. MC	<p>23da_dcdd</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Two Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the between a single pair of genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among two genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #9c392d;">Gene H</span></strong> is associated with the '<span style="color: #9c392d;"><i>hairy</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #9c392d;">Gene H</span> cells develop long, thread-like filaments that extend outward, creating a hairy, shaggy texture on the colony.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #006d61;">Gene K</span></strong> is linked with the '<span style="color: #006d61;"><i>knotted</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #006d61;">Gene K</span> cells grow in twisted, coiled shapes, resulting in a knotted or gnarled appearance.</li> </ul><table style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><tr><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 2px;"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="156" height="120" viewBox="0 0 122 94" role="img" aria-label="Unordered ascus: ++, hk, ++, hk"><desc>Each recessive allele contributes its own color; plus alleles remain neutral. style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 5px 8px;">3,400</td></tr></table><h6>Step-by-Step Instructions</h6><ul> <li>Step 1: Find the row for the Parental Type for all three genes.</li> <li>Step 2: Looking at only your two genes, assign PD, NPD, TT.</li> <li>Step 3: Determine if the two genes are linked.</li> <ul><li>PD &gt;&gt; NPD &rarr; linked; PD &approx; NPD &rarr; unlinked</li></ul> MC	<p>ff2f_a7f0</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Two Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the between a single pair of genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among two genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #0062a0;">Gene B</span></strong> is related to the '<span style="color: #0062a0;"><i>bubbly</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #0062a0;">Gene B</span> produces excessive gas bubbles during growth, causing foamy appearance of the media.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #993455;">Gene H</span></strong> is connected with the '<span style="color: #993455;"><i>hairy</i></span>' phenotype. MC	<p>ef29_ef09</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Two Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the between a single pair of genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among two genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #9c392d;">Gene F</span></strong> is analogous to the '<span style="color: #9c392d;"><i>fuzzy</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #9c392d;">Gene F</span> colonies are covered in soft, fine filaments, giving them a fuzzy, cotton-like texture.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #3c6c29;">Gene J</span></strong> is linked with the '<span style="color: #3c6c29;"><i>jeweled</i></span>' phenotype. MC	<p>8148_8dba</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Two Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the between a single pair of genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among two genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #5b640e;">Gene M</span></strong> is analogous to the '<span style="color: #5b640e;"><i>militant</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #5b640e;">Gene M</span> colonies are small, dense, and secrete compounds that inhibit the growth of nearby colonies.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #6141c2;">Gene W</span></strong> is linked with the '<span style="color: #6141c2;"><i>webbed</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #6141c2;">Gene W</span> colonies produce delicate, web-like strands that connect neighboring colonies in a cobweb pattern.</li> </ul><table style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><tr><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 2px;"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="156" height="120" viewBox="0 0 122 94" role="img" aria-label="Unordered ascus: ++, mw, ++, mw"><desc>Each recessive allele contributes its own color; plus alleles remain neutral. style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 5px 8px;">4,600</td></tr></table><h6>Step-by-Step Instructions</h6><ul> <li>Step 1: Find the row for the Parental Type for all three genes.</li> <li>Step 2: Looking at only your two genes, assign PD, NPD, TT.</li> <li>Step 3: Determine if the two genes are linked.</li> <ul><li>PD &gt;&gt; NPD &rarr; linked; PD &approx; NPD &rarr; unlinked</li></ul> <li>Step 4: Determine the map distance between the two genes.</li> <ul><li>D = &half; (TT + 6 NPD) / total = (3 NPD + &half; TT) / total</li></ul></ul><h5>Determine the distance between the two genes MC	<p>7945_7f6a</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Two Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the between a single pair of genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among two genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #0062a0;">Gene D</span></strong> is analogous to the '<span style="color: #0062a0;"><i>doubled</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #0062a0;">Gene D</span> cells display double or multiple budding, with several buds emerging simultaneously.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #993455;">Gene T</span></strong> is related to the '<span style="color: #993455;"><i>toxic</i></span>' phenotype. MC	<p>af7d_401b</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Two Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the between a single pair of genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among two genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #9c392d;">Gene H</span></strong> is linked with the '<span style="color: #9c392d;"><i>hairy</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #9c392d;">Gene H</span> cells develop long, thread-like filaments that extend outward, creating a hairy, shaggy texture on the colony.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #3c6c29;">Gene J</span></strong> is linked with the '<span style="color: #3c6c29;"><i>jeweled</i></span>' phenotype. MC	<p>e312_d927</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Two Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the between a single pair of genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among two genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #904610;">Gene E</span></strong> is correlated with the '<span style="color: #904610;"><i>elephant</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #904610;">Gene E</span> cells absorb excessive amounts of liquid, resulting in giant, swollen cells.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #006d61;">Gene M</span></strong> is correlated with the '<span style="color: #006d61;"><i>militant</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #006d61;">Gene M</span> colonies are small, dense, and secrete compounds that inhibit the growth of nearby colonies.</li> </ul><table style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><tr><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 2px;"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="156" height="120" viewBox="0 0 122 94" role="img" aria-label="Unordered ascus: ++, em, ++, em"><desc>Each recessive allele contributes its own color; plus alleles remain neutral. style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 5px 8px;">1,200</td></tr></table><h6>Step-by-Step Instructions</h6><ul> <li>Step 1: Find the row for the Parental Type for all three genes.</li> <li>Step 2: Looking at only your two genes, assign PD, NPD, TT.</li> <li>Step 3: Determine if the two genes are linked.</li> <ul><li>PD &gt;&gt; NPD &rarr; linked; PD &approx; NPD &rarr; unlinked</li></ul> <li>Step 4: Determine the map distance between the two genes.</li> <ul><li>D = &half; (TT + 6 NPD) / total = (3 NPD + &half; TT) / total</li></ul></ul><h5>Determine the distance between the two genes MC	<p>8b71_7f78</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Two Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the between a single pair of genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among two genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #5b640e;">Gene D</span></strong> is linked with the '<span style="color: #5b640e;"><i>doubled</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #5b640e;">Gene D</span> cells display double or multiple budding, with several buds emerging simultaneously.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #3456b9;">Gene Y</span></strong> is linked with the '<span style="color: #3456b9;"><i>yolk</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #3456b9;">Gene Y</span> cells develop a dense, yellowish core that resembles an egg yolk when viewed under a microscope.</li> </ul><table style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><tr><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 2px;"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="156" height="120" viewBox="0 0 122 94" role="img" aria-label="Unordered ascus: ++, dy, ++, dy"><desc>Each recessive allele contributes its own color; plus alleles remain neutral. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among two genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #006d61;">Gene D</span></strong> is connected with the '<span style="color: #006d61;"><i>doubled</i></span>' phenotype. MC	<p>aa07_fb25</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Two Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the between a single pair of genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among two genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #3c6c29;">Gene A</span></strong> is affiliated with the '<span style="color: #3c6c29;"><i>amber</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #3c6c29;">Gene A</span> cells develop a rich yellow-orange pigmentation, giving the colony a warm, amber hue.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #0062a0;">Gene H</span></strong> is linked with the '<span style="color: #0062a0;"><i>hairy</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #0062a0;">Gene H</span> cells develop long, thread-like filaments that extend outward, creating a hairy, shaggy texture on the colony.</li> </ul><table style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><tr><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 2px;"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="156" height="120" viewBox="0 0 122 94" role="img" aria-label="Unordered ascus: ++, ah, ++, ah"><desc>Each recessive allele contributes its own color; plus alleles remain neutral. MC	<p>08c4_8261</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Two Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the between a single pair of genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among two genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #9c392d;">Gene B</span></strong> is analogous to the '<span style="color: #9c392d;"><i>bubbly</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #9c392d;">Gene B</span> produces excessive gas bubbles during growth, causing foamy appearance of the media.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #3456b9;">Gene Y</span></strong> is correlated with the '<span style="color: #3456b9;"><i>yolk</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #3456b9;">Gene Y</span> cells develop a dense, yellowish core that resembles an egg yolk when viewed under a microscope.</li> </ul><table style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><tr><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 2px;"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="156" height="120" viewBox="0 0 122 94" role="img" aria-label="Unordered ascus: ++, by, ++, by"><desc>Each recessive allele contributes its own color; plus alleles remain neutral. MC	<p>a1fb_3bd5</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Two Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the between a single pair of genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among two genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #166e49;">Gene J</span></strong> is associated with the '<span style="color: #166e49;"><i>jeweled</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #166e49;">Gene J</span> colonies appear dotted with tiny, iridescent spots that sparkle under light.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #8f377b;">Gene K</span></strong> is correlated with the '<span style="color: #8f377b;"><i>knotted</i></span>' phenotype. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among two genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #5b640e;">Gene C</span></strong> is connected with the '<span style="color: #5b640e;"><i>clumpy</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #5b640e;">Gene C</span> grows in dense, irregular clusters, with cells clumping together rather than spreading smoothly.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #993455;">Gene K</span></strong> is associated with the '<span style="color: #993455;"><i>knotted</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #993455;">Gene K</span> cells grow in twisted, coiled shapes, resulting in a knotted or gnarled appearance.</li> </ul><table style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><tr><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 2px;"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="156" height="120" viewBox="0 0 122 94" role="img" aria-label="Unordered ascus: ++, ck, ++, ck"><desc>Each recessive allele contributes its own color; plus alleles remain neutral. MC	<p>ac19_6b08</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Two Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the between a single pair of genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among two genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #3c6c29;">Gene T</span></strong> is analogous to the '<span style="color: #3c6c29;"><i>toxic</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #3c6c29;">Gene T</span> secretes a toxic compound that inhibits or kills other microbial colonies nearby.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #6141c2;">Gene W</span></strong> is affiliated with the '<span style="color: #6141c2;"><i>webbed</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #6141c2;">Gene W</span> colonies produce delicate, web-like strands that connect neighboring colonies in a cobweb pattern.</li> </ul><table style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><tr><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 2px;"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="156" height="120" viewBox="0 0 122 94" role="img" aria-label="Unordered ascus: ++, tw, ++, tw"><desc>Each recessive allele contributes its own color; plus alleles remain neutral. MC	<p>9832_11b0</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Two Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the between a single pair of genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among two genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #715c00;">Gene E</span></strong> is correlated with the '<span style="color: #715c00;"><i>elephant</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #715c00;">Gene E</span> cells absorb excessive amounts of liquid, resulting in giant, swollen cells.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #3456b9;">Gene J</span></strong> is analogous to the '<span style="color: #3456b9;"><i>jeweled</i></span>' phenotype. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among two genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #166e49;">Gene A</span></strong> is correlated with the '<span style="color: #166e49;"><i>amber</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #166e49;">Gene A</span> cells develop a rich yellow-orange pigmentation, giving the colony a warm, amber hue.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #993455;">Gene W</span></strong> is connected with the '<span style="color: #993455;"><i>webbed</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #993455;">Gene W</span> colonies produce delicate, web-like strands that connect neighboring colonies in a cobweb pattern.</li> </ul><table style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><tr><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 2px;"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="156" height="120" viewBox="0 0 122 94" role="img" aria-label="Unordered ascus: ++, aw, ++, aw"><desc>Each recessive allele contributes its own color; plus alleles remain neutral. MC	<p>df59_bad5</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Two Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the between a single pair of genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among two genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #9c392d;">Gene N</span></strong> is affiliated with the '<span style="color: #9c392d;"><i>nude</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #9c392d;">Gene N</span> cells have an unusually smooth surface with no visible external features or textures.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #3456b9;">Gene R</span></strong> is connected with the '<span style="color: #3456b9;"><i>rusty</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #3456b9;">Gene R</span> colonies develop a reddish-brown pigmentation, reminiscent of rusted metal.</li> </ul><table style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><tr><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 2px;"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="156" height="120" viewBox="0 0 122 94" role="img" aria-label="Unordered ascus: ++, nr, ++, nr"><desc>Each recessive allele contributes its own color; plus alleles remain neutral. MC	<p>f701_d616</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Two Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the between a single pair of genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among two genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #9c392d;">Gene B</span></strong> is linked with the '<span style="color: #9c392d;"><i>bubbly</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #9c392d;">Gene B</span> produces excessive gas bubbles during growth, causing foamy appearance of the media.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #3c6c29;">Gene C</span></strong> is affiliated with the '<span style="color: #3c6c29;"><i>clumpy</i></span>' phenotype. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among two genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #166e49;">Gene C</span></strong> is analogous to the '<span style="color: #166e49;"><i>clumpy</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #166e49;">Gene C</span> grows in dense, irregular clusters, with cells clumping together rather than spreading smoothly.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #8f377b;">Gene N</span></strong> is analogous to the '<span style="color: #8f377b;"><i>nude</i></span>' phenotype. MC	<p>699d_bf60</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Two Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the between a single pair of genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among two genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #715c00;">Gene E</span></strong> is related to the '<span style="color: #715c00;"><i>elephant</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #715c00;">Gene E</span> cells absorb excessive amounts of liquid, resulting in giant, swollen cells.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #0062a0;">Gene M</span></strong> is affiliated with the '<span style="color: #0062a0;"><i>militant</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #0062a0;">Gene M</span> colonies are small, dense, and secrete compounds that inhibit the growth of nearby colonies.</li> </ul><table style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><tr><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 2px;"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="156" height="120" viewBox="0 0 122 94" role="img" aria-label="Unordered ascus: ++, em, ++, em"><desc>Each recessive allele contributes its own color; plus alleles remain neutral. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among two genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #5b640e;">Gene F</span></strong> is analogous to the '<span style="color: #5b640e;"><i>fuzzy</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #5b640e;">Gene F</span> colonies are covered in soft, fine filaments, giving them a fuzzy, cotton-like texture.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #006886;">Gene R</span></strong> is affiliated with the '<span style="color: #006886;"><i>rusty</i></span>' phenotype. MC	<p>1ef7_d020</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Two Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the between a single pair of genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among two genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #7f5411;">Gene R</span></strong> is linked with the '<span style="color: #7f5411;"><i>rusty</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #7f5411;">Gene R</span> colonies develop a reddish-brown pigmentation, reminiscent of rusted metal.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #3456b9;">Gene T</span></strong> is linked with the '<span style="color: #3456b9;"><i>toxic</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #3456b9;">Gene T</span> secretes a toxic compound that inhibits or kills other microbial colonies nearby.</li> </ul><table style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><tr><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 2px;"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="156" height="120" viewBox="0 0 122 94" role="img" aria-label="Unordered ascus: ++, rt, ++, rt"><desc>Each recessive allele contributes its own color; plus alleles remain neutral. MC	<p>43ca_62e9</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Two Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the between a single pair of genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among two genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #715c00;">Gene C</span></strong> is connected with the '<span style="color: #715c00;"><i>clumpy</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #715c00;">Gene C</span> grows in dense, irregular clusters, with cells clumping together rather than spreading smoothly.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #0062a0;">Gene K</span></strong> is associated with the '<span style="color: #0062a0;"><i>knotted</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #0062a0;">Gene K</span> cells grow in twisted, coiled shapes, resulting in a knotted or gnarled appearance.</li> </ul><table style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><tr><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 2px;"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="156" height="120" viewBox="0 0 122 94" role="img" aria-label="Unordered ascus: ++, ck, ++, ck"><desc>Each recessive allele contributes its own color; plus alleles remain neutral. MC	<p>c3fa_fee7</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Two Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the between a single pair of genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among two genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #904610;">Gene A</span></strong> is linked with the '<span style="color: #904610;"><i>amber</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #904610;">Gene A</span> cells develop a rich yellow-orange pigmentation, giving the colony a warm, amber hue.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #036a73;">Gene M</span></strong> is connected with the '<span style="color: #036a73;"><i>militant</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #036a73;">Gene M</span> colonies are small, dense, and secrete compounds that inhibit the growth of nearby colonies.</li> </ul><table style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><tr><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 2px;"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="156" height="120" viewBox="0 0 122 94" role="img" aria-label="Unordered ascus: ++, am, ++, am"><desc>Each recessive allele contributes its own color; plus alleles remain neutral. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among two genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #715c00;">Gene P</span></strong> is associated with the '<span style="color: #715c00;"><i>pebble</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #715c00;">Gene P</span> produces colonies with a rough, uneven surface that resembles a collection of tiny pebbles.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #7f38a2;">Gene X</span></strong> is correlated with the '<span style="color: #7f38a2;"><i>xenon</i></span>' phenotype. MC	<p>965a_20c8</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Two Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the between a single pair of genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among two genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #9c392d;">Gene M</span></strong> is linked with the '<span style="color: #9c392d;"><i>militant</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #9c392d;">Gene M</span> colonies are small, dense, and secrete compounds that inhibit the growth of nearby colonies.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #006886;">Gene Y</span></strong> is affiliated with the '<span style="color: #006886;"><i>yolk</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #006886;">Gene Y</span> cells develop a dense, yellowish core that resembles an egg yolk when viewed under a microscope.</li> </ul><table style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><tr><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 2px;"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="156" height="120" viewBox="0 0 122 94" role="img" aria-label="Unordered ascus: ++, my, ++, my"><desc>Each recessive allele contributes its own color; plus alleles remain neutral. MC	<p>3aab_b088</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Two Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the between a single pair of genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among two genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #3c6c29;">Gene W</span></strong> is analogous to the '<span style="color: #3c6c29;"><i>webbed</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #3c6c29;">Gene W</span> colonies produce delicate, web-like strands that connect neighboring colonies in a cobweb pattern.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #8f377b;">Gene X</span></strong> is connected with the '<span style="color: #8f377b;"><i>xenon</i></span>' phenotype. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among two genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #166e49;">Gene J</span></strong> is related to the '<span style="color: #166e49;"><i>jeweled</i></span>' phenotype. MC	<p>f014_5226</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Two Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the between a single pair of genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among two genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #904610;">Gene M</span></strong> is connected with the '<span style="color: #904610;"><i>militant</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #904610;">Gene M</span> colonies are small, dense, and secrete compounds that inhibit the growth of nearby colonies.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #006886;">Gene R</span></strong> is analogous to the '<span style="color: #006886;"><i>rusty</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #006886;">Gene R</span> colonies develop a reddish-brown pigmentation, reminiscent of rusted metal.</li> </ul><table style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><tr><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 2px;"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="156" height="120" viewBox="0 0 122 94" role="img" aria-label="Unordered ascus: ++, mr, ++, mr"><desc>Each recessive allele contributes its own color; plus alleles remain neutral. MC	<p>8167_01a5</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Two Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the between a single pair of genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among two genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #715c00;">Gene K</span></strong> is affiliated with the '<span style="color: #715c00;"><i>knotted</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #715c00;">Gene K</span> cells grow in twisted, coiled shapes, resulting in a knotted or gnarled appearance.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #6141c2;">Gene W</span></strong> is correlated with the '<span style="color: #6141c2;"><i>webbed</i></span>' phenotype. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among two genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #715c00;">Gene A</span></strong> is analogous to the '<span style="color: #715c00;"><i>amber</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #715c00;">Gene A</span> cells develop a rich yellow-orange pigmentation, giving the colony a warm, amber hue.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #6141c2;">Gene J</span></strong> is associated with the '<span style="color: #6141c2;"><i>jeweled</i></span>' phenotype. MC	<p>abc8_7498</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Two Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the between a single pair of genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among two genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #9c392d;">Gene F</span></strong> is correlated with the '<span style="color: #9c392d;"><i>fuzzy</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #9c392d;">Gene F</span> colonies are covered in soft, fine filaments, giving them a fuzzy, cotton-like texture.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #3c6c29;">Gene N</span></strong> is related to the '<span style="color: #3c6c29;"><i>nude</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #3c6c29;">Gene N</span> cells have an unusually smooth surface with no visible external features or textures.</li> </ul><table style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><tr><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 2px;"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="156" height="120" viewBox="0 0 122 94" role="img" aria-label="Unordered ascus: ++, fn, ++, fn"><desc>Each recessive allele contributes its own color; plus alleles remain neutral.
